# IconButton

A square button that holds one icon, for frequent actions in toolbars, cards and composers.

## Usage

```jsx
import { IconButton } from "naksha";

<IconButton label="Copy link" icon="link" onPress={copy} />
```

| Prop | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | required: the button's name for everyone who cannot see the icon | |
| `icon` | an icon name or a node | |
| `variant` | `ghost`, `secondary`, `primary` | `ghost` |
| `size` | `sm` (32), `md` (40), `lg` (48); 36, 44, 52 under touch | `md` |
| `isDisabled` | | `false` |
| `styles` | layout only (ADR 0009) | |

## Best practices

- Pair it with a Tooltip that says the same words as `label`. If the action is rare or important, use a Button with a visible label instead.
- `ghost` is the default (icon in `fg-muted`, `fg-default` on hover). `primary` for the single send or confirm in a composer. `secondary` when it sits beside secondary buttons.

## Content

The label is a verb phrase: "Copy link", "Remove Lease_2026.pdf". Name the object when there are several of the same button on screen.

## Anatomy and spacing

Sizes match Button heights: 32, 40, 48 (36, 44, 52 on touch). Icons are 16, 16, 20.

## States

Hover adds `state-hover`; a pointer press scales to 0.94 (a small target needs a slightly bigger squeeze to read); a keyboard press changes colour only. Focus is the system outline. Disabled keeps the shape and drops to `fg-disabled`.

## Accessibility

**What Naksha provides.** A real button built on React Aria, named by `label`; the icon is hidden from assistive tech. Works in Windows High Contrast.

**What the designer decides.** The label, and whether the action is clear enough without visible text.

**What the developer must not break.** Never ship an IconButton without `label`; TypeScript requires it.
